THIS BAIL APPLICATION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 17.01.2024, ALONG WITH Bail Appl..5325/2023, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 BAIL APPL. NOs. 5325 & 7011 OF 2023  4  COMMON ORDER
The applications are filed under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for orders of pre- arrest bail.
As the applications are arise out of the same crime, they are consolidated, jointly heard and being disposed of by this common order.

2. B.A.No.5325/2023 is filed by the 1st accused and B.A.No.7011/2023 is filed by the 3rd accused in Crime No.296/2023 of the Kasaba Police Station, Kozhikode, registered against the accused (three in number) for allegedly committing the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. The prosecution case, in brief, is that: KPB Nidhi Ltd, Kozhikode had filed a complaint before the Police, alleging that the accused 1 and 2 had approached them on 17.04.2023 for a gold take over loan from Chathankandathil Finance Ltd, Kottooli branch, with whom the accused 1 and 2 had jointly pledged 470.9 grams of gold ornaments.
An employee of the defacto BAIL APPL. NOs. 5325 & 7011 OF 2023 complainant went to the latter company and confirmed the existence of the loan.

Accordingly, the defacto complainant agreed to disburse an amount of Rs.21,19,000/- to the 1st accused as take over loan, because the 1st accused had stated that the entire gold ornaments belonged to him.

On the basis of the letter given by the 1st accused, the loan amount was transferred from the defacto complainant to the account of the 1 st accused, who undertook that the amount would be paid to the latter company.
But, after the loan was disbursed, the 1st accused immediately transferred the amount to the bank account of the 3rd accused.
Immediately, the defacto complainant got the account of the 1st accused freezed.
Yet, an amount of Rs.7/- lakh was fraudulently withdrawn by the 3rd accused.
Thus, the accused have committed the above offence.

4. Heard; Sri.K.Rakesh, Sri.A.Ranjith Narayanan, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners,
Smt.Neema T.V., the learned Public Prosecutor and Sri.K.T.Saju, the learned counsel appearing for the 2 nd BAIL APPL. NOs. 5325 & 7011 OF 2023 respondent/defacto complainant.
5. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioners in unison submitted that the petitioners are totally innocent of the accusations leveled against them.
They have no complicity in the crime.
The 1 st accused is made a scapegoat in the above transaction.
He is not a beneficiary.
The accused have no criminal antecedents.
They are willing to cooperate with the investigation and abide by any stringent conditions that may be imposed by this Court.
Hence, an order of pre-arrest bail may be passed.

sentences.text: The learned Public Prosecutor opposed the applications.
She contended that the investigation is only at the nascent stage.
The custodial interrogation of the petitioners is necessary for the fair and proper investigation of the crime.
The petitioners have criminal antecedents.
Hence, the applications may be dismissed.
7. The learned counsel appearing for the defacto complainant also opposed the applications.
He contended that the accused had the mens rea to cheat the defacto BAIL APPL. NOs. 5325 & 7011 OF 2023 complainant because they fabricated documents and mislead the defacto complainant.
Despite freezing the bank account of the 1st accused, an amount of Rs.7/- was still withdrawn by the 3rd accused.
Hence, the applications may be dismissed.

8. When the bail applications came up for consideration on 27.11.2023, this Court directed the Station House Officer to file a report to specify what had transpired in the crime after the dismissal of the applications filed by the petitioners before the Court of Sessions, Kozhikkode as Crl.M.C.Nos.953/2023 and 730/2023, especially since the 1st accused is a Civil Police Officer.

Subsequently, when the bail applications came up for consideration on 20.12.2023, this Court on finding that the Station House Officer had failed to comply with the directions passed by this Court within the stipulated time, suo-motu impleaded the District Police Chief, Kozhikode, as an additional respondent, and directed him to file a report regarding the investigation in the crime.
9.

Pursuant to the above order, the District Police BAIL APPL. NOs. 5325 & 7011 OF 2023 Chief,
Kozhikode has filed a detailed report dated 04.01.2024, inter-alia, stating that he has noticed laxity on the part of the Investigating Officer and now disciplinary proceedings have been initiated against the Station House Officer.
Consequent to the dismissal of the bail applications by the Court of Sessions, the investigation has not progressed.
The recovery has not been effected.
Even though the suspected locations were searched, it has not yielded fruitful results.
The 1 st accused is not a Civil Police Officer as claimed, but he is only an Office Assistant in the City Police Office at the time of the incident.
After the registration of the crime, he has been placed under suspension and a formal enquiry is in progress.
The custodial interrogation of the accused is necessary to detect the manner in which Rs.7/- lakh was withdrawn from the account of the 1st accused.
If the petitioners are granted an order of pre-arrest bail, it would hamper with the investigation.
Hence, the bail applications may be dismissed.
10. The prosecution allegation is that the accused 1 BAIL APPL. NOs. 5325 & 7011 OF 2023 to 3 with an intention to cheat the defacto complainant had approached them and sought for a take over loan.
After the loan was sanctioned, the 1st accused transferred the loan amount to the bank account of the 3rd accused, instead of the Finance Company.
Despite, the defacto complainant freezing the bank account of the 1 st accused, yet an amount of Rs.7/- lakh was withdrawn by the 3 rd accused through his bank account.

sentences.text: No inflexible guidelines or straitjacket formula can be provided for grant or refusal of anticipatory bail.

We are clearly of the view that no attempt should be made to provide rigid and inflexible guidelines in this respect because all circumstances and situations of future cannot be clearly visualised for the grant or refusal of anticipatory bail.
In consonance with the legislative intention the grant or refusal of anticipatory bail should necessarily depend on the facts and circumstances of each case.

As aptly observed in the Constitution Bench decision in Sibbia case [(1980) 2 SCC 565 : 1980 SCC (Cri) 465] that the High Court or the Court of Session has to exercise their jurisdiction under Section 438 CrPC by a wise and careful use of their discretion which by their long training and experience they are ideally suited to do.
In any event, this is the legislative mandate which we are bound to respect and honour.

112. The following factors and parameters can be taken into consideration while dealing with the anticipatory bail:
(i) The nature and gravity of the accusation and the exact role of the accused must be properly comprehended before arrest is made;

BAIL APPL. NOs. 5325 & 7011 OF 2023 (ii) The antecedents of the applicant including the fact as to whether the accused has previously undergone imprisonment on conviction by a court in respect of any cognizable offence;
The court must also clearly comprehend the exact role of the accused in the case.

sentences.text: (ix) The court to consider reasonable apprehension of tampering of the witness or apprehension of threat to the complainant;

(x) Frivolity in prosecution should always be considered and it is only the element of genuineness that shall have to be considered in the matter of grant of bail and in the event of there being some doubt as to the genuineness of the prosecution, in the normal course of events, the accused is entitled to an order of bail.

126. We deem it appropriate to reiterate and assert that discretion vested in the court in all matters should be exercised with care and circumspection depending upon the facts and circumstances justifying its exercise.
Similarly, the discretion vested with the court under Section 438 CrPC should also be exercised with caution and prudence.
It is unnecessary to travel beyond it and subject the wide power and discretion conferred by the legislature to a rigorous code of self-imposed limitations".

12. Likewise, in Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia v. State of BAIL APPL. NOs. 5325 & 7011 OF 2023 Punjab,
(1980) 2 SCC 565 ] the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held as follows:
"21.

sentences.text: The High Court says in its fourth proposition that in addition to the limitations mentioned in Section 437, the petitioner must make out a "special case" for the exercise of the power to grant anticipatory bail.
This, virtually, reduces the salutary power conferred by Section 438 to a dead letter.

In its anxiety, otherwise just, to show that the power conferred by Section 438 is not "unguided or uncanalised", the High Court has subjected that power to a restraint which will have the effect of making the power utterly unguided.
To say that the applicant must make out a "special case" for the exercise of the power to grant anticipatory bail is really to say nothing.
The applicant has undoubtedly to make out a case for the grant of anticipatory bail.
But one cannot go further and say that he must make out a "special case".
We do not see why the provisions of Section 438 should be suspected as containing something volatile or incendiary, which needs to be handled with the greatest care and caution imaginable.
A wise exercise of judicial power inevitably takes care of the evil consequences which are likely to flow out of its intemperate use.
Every kind of judicial discretion, whatever may be the nature of the matter in regard to which it is required to be exercised, has to be used with due care and caution.

In fact, an awareness of the context in which the discretion is required to be exercised and of the reasonably foreseeable consequences of its use, is the hallmark of a prudent exercise of judicial discretion.

One ought not to make a bugbear of the power to grant anticipatory bail".
13.

After bestowing my anxious consideration to the materials placed on record, particularly the report of the District Police Chief and the fact that the 1 st accused was an Office Assistant in the City Police Office and also taking note of the laxity on the part of the Investigating BAIL APPL. NOs.
5325 & 7011 OF 2023 Officer, which also is a matter to be investigated to ascertain whether the inaction was deliberate or not, and also the seriousness, gravity and nature of the accusations Bipin P vs The State Of Kerala on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9998107/
6 leveled against the petitioners, I am of the definite view that the petitioners are not entitled to invoke the extra ordinary jurisdiction of this Court under Sec.438 of the Code, especially when the custodial interrogation of the petitioners is necessary to conduct a fair and proper investigation and the investigation is only at a nascent stage.

sentences.text: Hence, I am not inclined to entertain these bail applications, which are devoid of any merits.
Consequentially, the bail applications are dismissed.

Nonetheless, I direct, in case the petitioners surrender before the Investigating Officer of the concerned Police Stations within a period of ten days from today, they shall be interrogated and,
thereafter, be produced before the jurisdictional Magistrates on the date of surrender itself.

Then, if the petitioners move an application for bail, the jurisdictional Court shall, untrammelled by any observations in this order, consider BAIL APPL. NOs. 5325 & 7011 OF 2023 the bail applications on their merits and as expeditiously as possible.

If the petitioners fail to surrender before the Investigating Officers as directed above, the Investigating Officers shall be free to arrest the petitioners, as if no order has been passed in these cases.
